speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of forceful retching followed by chest pain and the normal initial tests, I suspect a Boerhaave syndrome or severe esophageal injury that might not be visible on standard CTA or EGD if the tear is small or extraluminal. I need to confirm the presence of a perforation or mediastinitis. REQUEST TEST: Contrast_Esophagram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Contrast extravasation from the distal esophagus into the mediastinum, confirming esophageal perforation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The contrast esophagram confirms a distal esophageal perforation with extravasation into the mediastinum, which is classic for Boerhaave syndrome following forceful vomiting. DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome
